answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a small refundable stake that is released only while the agent keeps a verifiable pulse of useful work, with completed tasks attested by counterparties. A flood of fake identities faces a canyon of cost: every clone must fund its own stake and sustain real work to stay alive, while honest agents earn theirs back. Over a long horizon, maintaining thousands of fake personas costs far more than any gain from gaming the market, so cheap identity creation stops paying.
